questions.text: From bottom to top, the lines of the treble clef are...

answers.text: C) E, G, B, D, F

questions.text: From bottom to top, the spaces of the treble clef spell what word?
How many beats does a whole note last?
How many beats does a quarter note last?
The sign p in music tells you to play...
The sign f in music tells you to play...
Now that you finished Module 19: how well can you read the notes on the staff now? Answer in your own words.
How sure do you feel about reading the note names, the beats, and the loud-and-soft signs?
Is there one thing about reading music that still feels a little fuzzy? Tell us what it is so we can help.
I can name the lines (E, G, B, D, F) and spaces (FACE) on the treble clef.
I can tell how many beats whole, half, quarter, and eighth notes get.
Reading music takes perseverance, which means sticking with something even when it is hard. Tell about a time this week when you kept practicing instead of giving up.
Which word do we say for one quarter note?
We say "ti-ti" for...
How many beats does a dotted half note last?
A word or saying that helps you remember something is called a...
A rest means you stay quiet for that beat.
The pattern of long and short sounds in music is called the...
Now that you finished Module 20: how can tricks help us remember rhythms? Answer in your own words.
How sure do you feel about reading a rhythm using words like "ta" and "ti-ti"?
What is one thing about reading rhythms that still feels fuzzy to you? (It is okay if nothing does.)
I can say "ta" for a quarter note and "ti-ti" for two eighth notes.
I clapped and read a short rhythm pattern.
Reading rhythms takes perseverance, which means you keep trying even when it is tricky. Tell about a moment this week when you kept practicing a rhythm until it got easier.
What is K-Pop?

answers.text: A) A kind of drum from Africa
B) Popular music from South Korea
C) A type of dance from Mexico

questions.text: The planned dance moves a group does together are called...
The catchy part of a song that gets stuck in your head is the...
People enjoy K-Pop in many countries all around the world.
On the treble clef, the space notes spell which word?
Music notes on the staff are...

answers.text: B) the same all around the world
C) only used in South Korea

questions.text: This week's big question was: How is music the same all around the world? Answer in your own words.
How sure do you feel about what K-Pop is and reading more notes on the treble clef?
Is there anything from this week that still feels fuzzy or hard? Tell us so we can help.
I can explain what K-Pop is and where it comes from.
I can read more notes on the treble clef.

Courtesy means treating people and their ideas with kindness and respect. Enjoying music from other countries, like K-Pop from South Korea, is one way we show courtesy to people who are different from us. Tell about a time you enjoyed something from another country, or a song or food you would like to try.
What does a conductor do?

answers.text: C) Leads the musicians and keeps the beat

questions.text: The downbeat (beat 1) always moves which way?
A baton is...

answers.text: C) a thin stick the conductor holds

questions.text: How many beats are in 4/4 time?
The shape your hand makes as you mark the beats is called the...
The conductor helps all the musicians stay together on the same beat.
Now that you finished Module 22: how does a conductor help the music stay together? Answer in your own words.
How sure do you feel about conducting the 2/4, 3/4, and 4/4 patterns?
What part of conducting still feels a little fuzzy to you? (For example: the patterns, the downbeat, or counting the beats.)
I can explain what a conductor does and show that the downbeat moves down.
I conducted the 2/4, 3/4, and 4/4 patterns with my hand.

Keeping a steady beat takes self-government, which means controlling your own body and staying on track without anyone telling you. Tell about a time this week when you had to control your hand and your counting to keep the beat steady.
What does tempo tell us about the music?

answers.text: A) How high or low the notes are
B) How fast or slow the music goes
C) How loud the music is
D) How many singers there are

questions.text: A steady beat is most like...
How many beats are in the 4/4 beating pattern?
In 4/4 time, how many beats does a half note last?
The first beat of every beating pattern goes straight down.
What is a beating pattern?

answers.text: A) The words a singer sings
B) How loud or soft the music is
C) A list of your favorite songs
D) The shape your hand draws to show each beat

questions.text: This week's big question: Can you keep a steady beat while you conduct and read at the same time? Answer in your own words. How did it go for you?
How sure do you feel about keeping a steady tempo while you conduct and read note values?
Is anything still fuzzy for you? Maybe a beating pattern (2/4, 3/4, or 4/4), or how long a note lasts? Tell what you want to practice more.
I can mark the 2/4, 3/4, and 4/4 beating patterns with my hand.
I can read music with mixed note values while I keep the beat.
Keeping a steady beat takes perseverance, which means you keep trying even when it is hard and you do not give up. Tell about a moment this week when you kept practicing until something got easier.
Which group lists the four main string instruments?

answers.text: B) Violin, viola, cello, double bass

questions.text: Drawing a bow across the strings is called...
Plucking the strings with your finger is called...
Which section is the largest in the orchestra?
Antonio Vivaldi wrote famous music called The Four Seasons.
Which is the smallest string instrument that plays the highest notes?
Now that you finished Module 24: what makes the string family special? Answer in your own words.
How sure do you feel about the string family and the two ways strings make sound (arco and pizzicato)?
Is anything still fuzzy or tricky about the strings, Vivaldi, or the conducting patterns? Tell us what, so we can help.
I can name the four main string instruments.
I can show the 2/4, 3/4, and 4/4 conducting patterns.

The strings are the largest section, and they work together to serve the whole orchestra and make it sound full and beautiful. That is the virtue of service: helping a group be its best. Tell about one time you helped a group you are part of, like your family, your class, or a team.
Which string instrument is the smallest and plays the highest notes?
The viola is a little bigger than the violin. How does it sound?
Which clef do both the violin and the viola read?
What does a player draw across the strings to make a sound?
You hold both the violin and the viola under your chin.
What is rosin used for?

answers.text: D) To help the bow grip the strings

questions.text: Now that you finished Module 25: how are the violin and viola alike, and how are they different? Answer in your own words.
How sure do you feel about telling the violin and viola apart by size and sound?
Is anything still fuzzy about the violin, the viola, the treble clef, or the parts (bow, bridge, rosin)? Tell us what you would like to go over again.
I can tell which instrument is smaller and plays higher (violin) and which is bigger and plays lower (viola).
I know that both the violin and the viola read the treble clef.
Learning an instrument takes perseverance, which means you keep practicing even when something is hard. Tell about a part of this week's practice exercise that was tricky and how you kept going.
How do you hold a cello to play it?

answers.text: C) Sitting down, between your knees

questions.text: Which string instrument is the biggest and the lowest?
What word means plucking the strings with your fingers?
The deep, low notes of the double bass give the orchestra its...
The cello has a rich, warm sound.
On the treble clef, the four spaces from bottom to top spell what word?
Now that you finished Module 26: why does an orchestra need low instruments like the cello and the double bass? Answer in your own words.
How sure do you feel about telling the cello and the double bass apart and knowing how they sound?
Is anything still fuzzy or confusing about the cello, the double bass, or reading treble clef notes? Tell us so we can help.
I can describe how the cello is played and how it sounds.
I can explain why the double bass gives the orchestra its deep foundation.

The low instruments do not always get the spotlight, but they serve the whole orchestra by holding up the sound underneath everyone else. Tell about a time you helped or served your family, your class, or a friend, even when no one noticed.
How is the flute played?

answers.text: C) Held sideways and blown across a hole
D) Blow through a double reed

questions.text: What gives the oboe its thin, reedy sound?
Which family do the flute and the oboe belong to?
In Peter and the Wolf, which instrument plays the bird?
A leap of a third...

answers.text: A) stays on the same note
C) moves to the very next note

questions.text: Prokofiev gave each character in Peter and the Wolf its own instrument.
Now that you finished Module 27: How can instruments tell a story? Answer in your own words.
How sure do you feel about telling the flute and the oboe apart, and reading a leap of a third?
Is anything still fuzzy or tricky about the woodwinds, Prokofiev, or thirds? Tell us what, so we can help.
I can tell the flute and the oboe apart by how they are played and how they sound.
I can read a leap of a third on the staff.
Making a video where you talk and read note names out loud takes courage. Tell how it felt to record yourself for this assignment.
The clarinet makes its sound with a...
Which woodwind is the lowest one, with a deep, buzzy sound?
The bassoon makes its sound with a...
An interval that steps to the very next note is a...
An interval that skips one note is a...
Which instrument has the fun nickname "licorice stick"?
Now that you finished Module 28: how do woodwinds make their different sounds? Answer in your own words.
How sure do you feel about the clarinet, the bassoon, and naming a 2nd or a 3rd?
Is anything still a little fuzzy from this week? Tell me what you would like to go over again. (If nothing is fuzzy, that is great too.)
I can tell a single reed from a double reed.
I can name an interval as a 2nd or a 3rd.

Learning to hear the difference between two reeds and two intervals takes perseverance, which means sticking with something even when it is tricky. Tell about a moment this week when you kept trying until something made sense.
How do brass players make a sound?

answers.text: A) By hitting drums with sticks
B) By buzzing their lips into a mouthpiece

questions.text: Which instrument is the smallest and highest in the brass family?
How many valves does a trumpet have?
What does a sharp do to a note?
What does a flat do to a note?
Which accidental cancels a sharp or a flat and puts the note back to normal?
Now that you finished Module 29: how do brass players and accidentals change the sound? Answer in your own words.
How sure do you feel about the trumpet and the three accidentals?
Is anything still fuzzy or tricky about the brass family or accidentals? Tell us what, so we can help.
I can explain how brass players make a sound and name the trumpet.
I can tell what a sharp, a flat, and a natural do to a note.
Trying a new sound, like buzzing your lips or drawing a brand-new symbol, takes courage. Tell about a moment this week when you tried something new even though it felt a little hard.
The French horn is what kind of instrument?
The long tubing on a French horn is...
While playing, the French horn player keeps one hand...
The French horn is known for a sound that is...
A sharp does what to a note?
A natural sign does what?

answers.text: C) Raises a note two steps
D) Cancels a sharp or a flat

questions.text: Now that you finished Module 30: what makes the French horn special and tricky? Answer in your own words.
How sure do you feel about the French horn and reading sharps, flats, and naturals?
Was anything still fuzzy this week? It is okay to say so. Tell us one thing you would like to go over again.
I can describe the French horn and tell why it is tricky to play.
I can tell what a sharp, a flat, and a natural do to a note.

The French horn is one of the trickiest instruments to play, and reading accidentals takes practice too. Perseverance means we keep trying even when something is hard. Tell about a time this week you kept going even when the work felt tricky.
What makes the trombone different from every other brass instrument?

answers.text: A) It has the most valves
B) It uses a slide instead of valves
C) It is the smallest brass instrument
D) It is made of wood

questions.text: The smooth slide from one note to another on a trombone is called a...
How many slide positions does the trombone have?
What does a sharp do to a note?

answers.text: C) Puts it back to normal

questions.text: Which accidental puts a note back to its normal sound?
The trombone has a bold, powerful sound.
Now that you finished Module 31: how is the trombone different from every other brass instrument? Answer in your own words.
How sure do you feel about the trombone and reading notes with accidentals?
Is there anything that still feels fuzzy or tricky this week? Tell us what you would like more practice with. (It is okay to say "nothing.")
I can explain how the trombone uses a slide instead of valves.
I can read notes out loud, including notes with accidentals.
Reading notes out loud from memory takes perseverance, which means sticking with something even when it feels hard. Tell about a moment this week when you kept trying and did not give up.
Which brass instrument is the biggest and lowest?
What is the wide, open end of the tuba called, where the sound comes out?
What does ear training mean?

answers.text: C) Reading music with your eyes
D) Learning to hear differences in music

questions.text: Music that is major often sounds...
Music that is minor often sounds...

answers.text: C) dark or a little sad

questions.text: What do we call the space between two notes?
This week's big question was: How can our ears tell happy music from sad music? Answer in your own words.
How sure do you feel about telling when music sounds major (happy) or minor (sad)?
Is there anything about the tuba or about major and minor sounds that still feels fuzzy or confusing? Tell us what, so we can help.
I can describe the tuba and tell why it is special in the brass family.
I can tell when music sounds major (happy) or minor (sad).

Careful listening takes self-government, which means staying calm and paying close attention even when it is hard. Tell about a time this week when you slowed down and really listened. How did it help you hear the difference between happy and sad sounds?
The percussion family is anything you can...
Which one is PITCHED percussion that can play real notes?
Which one is UNPITCHED percussion that just makes a sound?
A major scale is a row of eight notes that sounds...
The C major scale on a piano uses all the...
A snare drum can play a whole tune like Do-Re-Mi.
Now that you finished Module 33: how is percussion different from the other families? Answer in your own words.
How sure do you feel about telling pitched percussion from unpitched percussion and singing a major scale?
Is there anything about percussion or the major scale that still feels fuzzy or tricky? Tell us so we can help.
I can tell pitched percussion from unpitched percussion.
I sang a major scale going up.
Singing a whole scale and getting every note right takes perseverance, which means to keep trying even when something is hard. Tell about a moment this week when you kept trying until you got it.
How many beats does a quarter note get in 4/4 time?
Which note value lasts the longest?
A rest in music tells you to...
In a 4/4 time signature, how many beats are in each measure?
The lines of the treble clef, from bottom to top, are E, G, B, D, F. Which saying helps you remember them?

answers.text: A) Every Good Boy Does Fine
D) Good Boys Do Fine Always

questions.text: The four spaces of the treble clef spell which word?
Now that you finished your first review week: what part of music do you understand best now? Answer in your own words.
How sure do you feel about rhythm, note values, and reading the treble clef staff?
Is there one part of this week's review that still feels fuzzy or tricky? Tell us what it is so we can help.
I can name the note values (whole, half, quarter, eighth) and the beats each one gets.
I can name the lines and spaces of the treble clef staff.
Reviewing on your own takes self-government, which means guiding yourself to do the work even when no one is watching. Tell how you guided yourself to review this week. What helped you stay on track?
Which word means the tune you can hum or sing?
What do dynamics tell us in music?

answers.text: A) The name of the song
C) How long the music is
D) How loud or soft to play

questions.text: A crescendo means the music...
Which composer kept writing music even when he could not hear well?
On the treble clef, the space notes from bottom to top spell which word?
Rhythm, melody, harmony, and tone are all parts of music.
Now that you finished Module 35: which musician or music idea will you remember most, and why? Answer in your own words.
How sure do you feel about the parts of music, music symbols, and the composers you met?
Is there anything from this review week that still feels fuzzy or hard to remember? Tell us what, so we can help.
I can name some parts of music, like rhythm, melody, harmony, and tone.
I can remember some composers or musicians I met this year.
Reviewing and remembering what you learned takes responsibility. Tell one way you took responsibility for your own learning this week.
How many instrument families are there in an orchestra?
A drum belongs to which instrument family?
A sad-sounding tune in music is called...
Which accidental makes a note a little lower?
A natural sign takes away a sharp or a flat and brings the note back to plain.
What does a conductor do?

answers.text: B) Leads the music and shows the beat

questions.text: This was your last big review of the year. What is one music idea you feel proud to know now? Answer in your own words.
How sure do you feel about the four instrument families, happy and sad sounds, accidentals, and conducting?
Is there one topic from this week that still feels fuzzy to you? Tell which one, so your teacher can help.
I can name the four instrument families.
I can tell when music sounds happy (major) or sad (minor).
Being a good music listener means showing courtesy: we listen quietly and clap when someone shares their music. Tell about a time you showed courtesy while someone played or sang.
Think back to the very beginning of the year. What is something about music you understand now that you did not understand back then?
How do you feel as a music scholar now?
What was your favorite thing we learned this year? (An instrument, a composer, a song, a music word, anything!)
I can name instruments from the four families (strings, woodwinds, brass, percussion).
I can read notes on the treble clef staff.
I can hear feelings in music (loud/soft, fast/slow, happy/sad).
You worked hard all year long, which takes perseverance. What are you most proud of learning in music this year?
Leave a short message about your year in music class. This is your final check-in for the year. Have a wonderful summer, music scholar!
